title: Ravel
description: Ravel's own ravel_* families, grouped by the subsystem that renders them. services/ravel-server/tests/shipped_rules_name_emitted_metrics.rs asserts every metric name a target here references appears on a # TYPE line of a rendered /metrics body.

panels.title: Acknowledged writes
panels.description: Requests Ravel answered, split by whether the write was durable. A rising err rate with a flat ok rate is the shape a store outage takes at the ingest surface.

panels.title: Admission decisions
panels.description: Admitted data against the admission-control rejections, by the reason ADR-0051 names. RavelStructuralRejections and RavelEventTimeSkew alert on the reason= dimension of the second target.

panels.title: Ingest bytes
panels.description: Wire bytes as received against the bytes admission charged. The two differ by whatever the transport decompressed; neither is a count of bytes written to object storage.

panels.title: Flushes by trigger
panels.description: Which condition closed each segment. A fleet flushing almost entirely by age is writing small objects and will read slowly.

panels.title: Flush concurrency
panels.description: Flushes in flight against the seconds writers spent waiting for a flush permit. Permit wait climbing while in-flight sits at the configured maximum is the ceiling being reached.

panels.title: Ingest buffer and shedding
panels.description: Buffered bytes against the configured limit, with the two shed counters. Shedding with the buffer well under its limit points at the concurrency limiter, not at the byte budget.

panels.title: Active series and write faults
panels.description: Cardinality under admission control, and the four ingest faults that are never routine. A nonzero partial-write or shard-death rate means data was acknowledged and then lost a writer.

panels.title: Queries
panels.description: Completed queries across every read surface.

panels.title: Object-store work per read
panels.description: Requests and bytes the read path issued. The two byte series count different things: s3_bytes is bytes as transferred, decompressed_bytes is what those bytes expanded to, so they must not be summed.

panels.title: Planner estimates
panels.description: What the planner charged against the query budget before the scan ran. Compare each against its actual on the panel to the left: an estimate far under the actual is a budget that cannot refuse the query it should have refused.

panels.title: Query result cache hit ratio
panels.description: Hits over hits plus misses. The denominator is floored at 1e-9, below any real rate, so an idle fleet reads 0 without understating a real ratio rather than dropping the series.

panels.title: Object cache traffic
panels.description: The block cache under the query path, split by the cache= family that serves each lookup.

panels.title: Cache residency and disk tier
panels.description: How full the cache is, what it serves, and the two disk-tier degradations. A nonzero degraded-to-miss rate means the disk tier is failing reads and the cache is silently behaving as a smaller one.

panels.title: Log block pruning
panels.description: The share of log blocks the postings index pruned before decode, and the blocks that survived to be scanned. A pruned share falling towards zero is the postings index stopping to pay for itself. The denominator is floored at 1e-9, below any real rate, so an idle fleet reads 0 without understating a real ratio rather than dropping the series.

panels.title: Fold age by signal
panels.description: Seconds since any process last completed a fold of this signal. RavelCatalogFoldStalled pages on this crossing 4800s for 10m; the unsealed ingest span grows for as long as it climbs.

panels.title: Fold cycles and failures
panels.description: A fold that is running and failing shows here before the age panel to the left crosses its threshold.

panels.title: Declared-stat stamp coverage
panels.description: Stamped carriers read against stamped snapshot entries written, over the hour RavelFoldStampCoverageShortfall uses. Records above entries means stamps are being dropped, and the drop counter names the carrier to look at.

panels.title: Catalog integrity
panels.description: Three counters that must stay flat at zero. Any of them moving is a correctness event, not a capacity one.

panels.title: Maintenance cycle age
panels.description: Seconds since this process completed a maintenance cycle. Not aggregated across replicas on purpose: unit ownership is partitioned (ADR-0065), so a single dead loop strands its own units while its peers stay fresh.

panels.title: Workers and units
panels.description: Live maintenance workers, the units they own, the units that stalled, and the L0 records still waiting to be folded in.

panels.title: Tenant coverage
panels.description: Tenants discovered against tenants actually maintained. A gap means some tenant's retention, compaction and GC are not running at all.

panels.title: Orphans
panels.description: Objects the sweeper found unreferenced, what it withheld inside the safety window, and the quarantine flow. A refused quarantine is an object the sweeper wanted to move and could not.

panels.title: Reclaim and safety brakes
panels.description: Physical deletes by kind, against the four brakes that stop the sweeper. The breaker, the conservation aborts and the loop panics each mean reclaim stopped on purpose or on a crash, not that there was nothing to reclaim.

panels.title: Merge memory and process budget
panels.description: The k-way merge high-water marks against the ADR-1170 process budget. component= on the reserved gauge is not yet a real split: SQL reserves the whole process total today, so the two components must not be summed.

panels.title: Store reachability
panels.description: The store probe's verdict, taken as a minimum so one unreachable replica is visible rather than averaged away.

panels.title: Probe failures, cycle age and bucket protection
panels.description: Probe failures, how long ago the probe last completed a cycle, and whether Ravel could establish that the bucket is versioned and protected. The cycle age is the liveness signal: the failure counter and the protection gauge both move only while the probe task is alive, so a dead task freezes them at a healthy-looking value while the age keeps climbing. An unknown protection state is not a safe state.

panels.title: Store latency p99 by op
panels.description: The 99th percentile of the ravel_store_latency_seconds histogram, per object-store operation.

panels.title: Store calls, attempts and errors
panels.description: Calls are logical operations; attempts are billed HTTP requests, so attempts above calls is expected (a multipart write or a ranged read issues several) and is not a retry count.

panels.title: Store bytes and mean latency
panels.description: Bytes as transferred per operation, and the histogram's own mean. The denominator is floored at 1e-9, below any real rate, so an operation with no calls in the window reads 0 without understating a real mean.

panels.title: Scrub and tenancy integrity
panels.description: The background scrub's three disagreement counters, its cursor, and the two provisioning and tenancy counters that say a process adopted state it should not have. Every series here is expected to stay flat at zero except the cursor.

panels.title: Durable auth and audit
panels.description: The durable token cache's refresh health, and audit write failures. Failing closed on stale state rejects live traffic; a failing audit write means a request was served with no durable record of it.

panels.title: Alert tick age
panels.description: Seconds since the alert evaluator last completed a tick. RavelAlertLoopStalled pages on this crossing 600s for 15m.

panels.title: Tick outcomes
panels.description: How each evaluation tick ended. lease_not_held is the steady state of every replica that is not the lease holder and is not a fault; history_unavailable and lease_unavailable are.

panels.title: Rule evaluations
panels.description: Rules evaluated against rules that failed to evaluate. A failing rule fires nothing and reports nothing on its own.

panels.title: Notification delivery
panels.description: Deliveries against failures. Failures rising while deliveries sit at zero is the shape RavelAlertNotificationsAllFailing pages on.

panels.title: Alert records and repeats
panels.description: Alert state records durably written, and repeat notifications queued behind them.
